title: Fibonacci proteins on the triangular lattice
statement: In the HP model of protein folding a chain of hydrophobic (H) and polar (P) monomers occupies distinct sites of a lattice, consecutive monomers on neighbouring sites, and its energy is minus the number of pairs of H monomers that are lattice neighbours without being consecutive. Take the Fibonacci words S_1 = P, S_2 = H, S_k = S_(k-1) S_(k-2) (S_3 = HP, S_4 = HPH, S_5 = HPHHP, ...; S_k has length F_k) as sequences and the triangular lattice (each site has 6 neighbours) as the lattice. Determine the ground-state energy E_k of S_k. The headline cell is S_10, of length 55: find a conformation with energy below -44.
submission: Text file: 55 lines 'a b', the lattice site a + b e^(i pi/3) of each monomer in chain order (neighbouring sites differ by (1,0), (0,1), (-1,1), (-1,0), (0,-1) or (1,-1)).
score: the energy, minus the number of non-consecutive H-H neighbour pairs (smaller is better)

best_known.source: Quantavane (Arhan Canli), 9 November 2026: simulated annealing with pivot moves over self-avoiding conformations (tools/hp_tri.py, two runs of 60 s)

context: The HP model (Dill 1985; Lau and Dill 1989) is the standard minimal model of protein folding and a standard hard benchmark for optimisation (finding HP ground states is NP-hard on the square and cubic lattices); its benchmark sequences are mostly random or designed. Fibonacci sequences are the canonical quasiperiodic chains: Stillinger, Head-Gordon and Hirshfeld introduced them for the off-lattice AB model, where they remain test cases for folding algorithms (e.g. cond-mat/0302545), but they have not been posed as HP chains on a lattice. On the triangular lattice the model is less constrained by parity than on the square lattice (odd cycles exist, so any two monomers can touch), and the question is how a quasiperiodic hydrophobic pattern packs: the H fraction of S_k tends to 1/phi = 0.618..., and the best folds found put the H monomers into a compact core.
references: K. A. Dill, Theory for the folding and stability of globular proteins, Biochemistry 24 (1985) 1501-1509
K. F. Lau, K. A. Dill, A lattice statistical mechanics model of the conformational and sequence spaces of proteins, Macromolecules 22 (1989) 3986-3997
F. H. Stillinger, T. Head-Gordon, C. L. Hirshfeld, Toy model for protein folding, Phys. Rev. E 48 (1993) 1469-1477 (Fibonacci sequences in the AB model)
Structure optimization in an off-lattice protein model, arXiv:cond-mat/0302545 (Fibonacci AB chains, off-lattice)

novelty.verdict: new. No ground-state energies of Fibonacci HP chains on any lattice were found (arXiv, web search); Fibonacci sequences have been folded only in the off-lattice AB model, and triangular-lattice HP studies use other sequences.
closest: Fibonacci sequences in the off-lattice AB model (Stillinger et al. 1993; Hsu et al., cond-mat/0302545): the same sequences in a different, continuous model.
HP folding on the triangular lattice (e.g. cond-mat/9708049): the same lattice with other sequences.

first_values.note: Exact values: every self-avoiding conformation enumerated (tools/hp_tri.py exact); larger chains: our best annealed folds (upper bounds). S_10 has 34 H and 21 P monomers.

baseline.text: -44 for S_10 (length 55), held by Quantavane (Arhan Canli), 9 November 2026: the fold in `refs/hp-tri.txt`. Lower bound -69: each H monomer has at most 4 neighbouring sites besides its chain neighbours (5 at a chain end), so 34 H monomers make at most 69 contacts.

bound.source: at most 4 free neighbours per H monomer (5 at an end); 34 H monomers
